title: Persons entitled to fill an order for Schedule I or II substances
rule_summary: An order for Schedule I and II controlled substances, whether on a DEA Form 222 or an electronic order, may be filled only by a person registered with DEA as a manufacturer or distributor of substances listed in Schedule I or II, or as an importer of such substances, except for the cases 21 CFR 1305.06 lists. Among those cases: a person registered with DEA to dispense or export the substances may, if discontinuing business or if the registration is expiring without reregistration, dispose of Schedule I or II substances in its possession with a DEA Form 222 or electronic order in accordance with 21 CFR 1301.52; a purchaser who obtained a Schedule I or II substance by a DEA Form 222 or electronic order may return the substance to the supplier of the substance with a DEA Form 222 or electronic order from the supplier; and a person registered to dispense Schedule II substances may distribute them to another dispenser with a DEA Form 222 or electronic order only in the circumstances described in 21 CFR 1307.11.
exam_relevance: Tests whether the candidate can see that a dispensing pharmacy is sometimes the party filling an order rather than the party placing one, which is what brings the supplier-side duties on an order form into a pharmacy's practice.

authority.name: Persons entitled to fill orders for Schedule I and II controlled substances

common_confusions: A pharmacy is the purchaser on the order it places to stock the shelf and the supplier on the order that moves that stock back out.
The dispenser-to-dispenser distribution route is confined to the circumstances 21 CFR 1307.11 describes.
verification_notes: Read in the current eCFR text of 21 CFR 1305.06 on ecfr.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed. A fresh independent audit is still required before any section relying on it is published.
